items.title: Mrs. Arnold Metoyer Interview, 1960-10-19
items.q: They say he played that film so beautiful, Willie Pazzo.

ctx.x: A week before he died. And during the flu, he was very, very sick. So the doctor told him, he said, now that they were, he was framed with the doctor, you know, and the doctor said, listen, let me tell you something, I know. He said, you're a very, very sick man. And I'm going to pat you up. And I want you to stop smoking, stop drinking, and stop that home. He said, well, doc, I'll stop the smoking, I'll stop the drinking, but I'm going to play until I drop dead. Yeah, he did too. Yeah. Play until he couldn't go…

Something like Willie. They said that day before, he played that film the day before he died, you know. They say he played that film so beautiful, Willie Pazzo. Oh, Willie Pazzo. They say he played them hymns and played that film like if nothing wasn't wrong with him at all. And the next morning. Yeah, the very night, really during the night. That's right.

And when he used to come and serenade us at 2 o'clock in the morning, where we live now, visit the sacred heart conference. Well, the nuns used to tell the children, the boys, you know, and they were living right in the back of them, who was playing the music last night? He said, we certainly did enjoy that music. It was fine. It was fine. Nobody in the neighborhood complained about him playing. They used to play so low with those music. Yes. You know, it was pretty. It was really pretty. With the old, I mean,…
